name: Heartbeat
tagline: Run a private community with channels, events, courses, and lightweight workflows

tiers.name: Build
tiers.limits: Up to 350 members; 5 workflows; 1 landing page; 256 video-room attendees; unlimited room hours; 5% platform transaction fee

tiers.name: Grow
tiers.limits: Up to 5,000 members; unlimited workflows; 15 landing pages; 50 native-video hours/month; 256 video-room attendees; 2.5% platform transaction fee

tiers.name: Scale
tiers.limits: Unlimited members; 50 landing pages; 200 native-video hours/month; 256 video-room attendees; 1.25% platform transaction fee

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day trial with no credit card
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual totals are $490, $1,490 and $9,200
pricing.hiddenCosts: Platform transaction fees of 5%/2.5%/1.25% are added to payment-processor fees (Heartbeat illustrates Stripe at about 2.9% + $0.30). Build can add 50 native-video hours for $19/month. Admins and moderators count toward the member cap.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Heartbeat, run a private community with channels, events, courses, and lightweight workflows. The hard boundary is mobile apps, automations, analytics, payments, and community onboarding, plus network, moderation, and communication infrastructure.
coreLoopDIY: Host a private community with channels, events, courses, and lightweight workflows, organize discussion by topic, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
whatYouLose: mobile apps, automations, analytics, payments, and community onboarding
ongoingBurden: realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Heartbeat because community software is valuable when members are already there and the operator does not have to own realtime reliability and abuse response. The recurring cost buys realtime delivery, notifications, abuse handling, search, media, permissions, mobile clients, backups, and community operations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Discourse
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source community discussion platform with strong moderation and search.

alternatives.name: Moodle
alternatives.desc: Courses, forums, events and completion rules in one mature system; it feels like a school because it is one.

rejectedAlternatives.name: HumHub
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Spaces, events and workflows are real, but courses and creator payments are not part of the free core.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Odoo Community
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The required modules exist, but asking a member to join your ERP is not a community strategy.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Build plan and a single private community DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Heartbeat in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, WebSockets, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: host a private community with channels, events, courses, and lightweight workflows, organize discussion by topic, and keep membership and moderation under the owner's control.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement spaces, channels, topics, replies, reactions, mentions, profiles, roles, and invitations.
Use WebSockets for live updates but preserve every message transactionally in PostgreSQL.
Add moderation queues, reports, blocks, rate limits, attachment limits, and an audit log.
Provide email digests, browser notifications, search, pinned content, and member export.
Add owner-controlled retention, account deletion, backup, restore, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with a seeded demo, migrations, and an emergency admin command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out public-network discovery and existing member liquidity.
Deliberately leave out production voice or video rooms.
Deliberately leave out native mobile applications, enterprise SSO, and 24-hour abuse operations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
